title: Training: the job lifecycle from one manifest
purpose: Submit a two-node training job with the golden-path manifest. All its pods must be admitted together, land in one zone, train, checkpoint, and finish. A job that does not fit must not start at all.

kubectl create -f trainjob.yaml   # s03-big: 3 nodes x 1 GPU. The training queue owns 2 GPUs.

checks.description: the 3-GPU job is held back with no pods at all, not started partially
checks.because: Kueue admits a TrainJob's whole PodSet or none of it. The queue owns 2 GPUs and the job needs 3.

checks.description: Kueue says why: insufficient quota in the training flavor
checks.because: The Workload's own condition message names the missing resource.

checks.description: both pods of the job were created at the same moment, after admission
checks.because: Kueue unsuspends the whole job on admission, so JobSet creates all pods together.

checks.description: both nodes are in the same availability zone
checks.because: The runtime's pod template requires pod affinity on the zone, so the second pod joins the first pod's zone.

checks.description: Prometheus is scraping live training metrics from both ranks
checks.because: The runtime's pod template carries scrape annotations; Prometheus discovers the pods through the API server.
The TrainJob reports Complete when every pod exits cleanly.

checks.description: each node ran a GPU burn-in before training and passed
checks.because: The training script multiplies large matrices on the GPU first and refuses to start if the result is not finite.
Loss fell from 2.6714 to 2.0121: the model learned from the dataset in S3.

checks.description: the final checkpoint has both ranks' shards and both completion markers
checks.because: Each rank writes its own shard, then its marker; a checkpoint counts only when every marker exists.
